questions.q: Why does social media give a false picture of relationships?
a: It shows only curated moments, not the daily struggle
It features mostly people who are single
It encourages readers to marry too young
It ignores the value of friendship
questions.why: Lesson 1 says the hashtag hides the mess and conflict that every relationship contains.

questions.q: What did the author tell Sarah about her list of requirements?
a: Her expectations were too unrealistic
She should lower her standards completely
She needed to date more casually first
She should wait until she was older
questions.why: Lesson 1 says her long, strict list of traits made her goals unrealistic.

questions.q: Why does the summary call singleness an important stage?
a: It builds the foundation for later relationships
It proves that you do not need anyone
It guarantees a better partner later
It should be kept as short as possible
questions.why: Lesson 2 says singleness is where you get to know yourself and your purpose first.

questions.q: Which six relationship stages does the summary list?
a: Singleness, dating, engagement, marriage, love, children
Dating, love, engagement, marriage, children, singleness
Singleness, engagement, dating, marriage, children, love
Dating, singleness, marriage, engagement, love, children
questions.why: Lesson 2 gives that order and stresses that singleness comes before the rest.

questions.q: What does the summary say about the work of marriage?
a: It begins, rather than ends, after the wedding
It fades once children arrive
It is easiest in the first years
It requires less effort over time
questions.why: Lesson 3 says marriage is where the hardest relational work starts, not where it stops.
